title: A game code for a review can be income
label: Creator Tax Check

hook.text: Got a *GTA VI* code to review it?

items.l: "It was a gift, so it's not income"
Paid in goods for a review = income
Count it at what it's worth

items.t: Game codes sent for a review
Gear a brand sends for a video

beats.text: Keep a list: *what* you got, *when*, and its value.
beats.sub: No form needed for it to count.

captions.instagram:
Got a GTA VI code from a publisher to review it? 🎮

Myth: "It was a gift, so it isn't income."
Fact: when you get goods or property in exchange for your work (a review, a video, a shout-out), the IRS treats it as income, form or no form.

✔️ Count it at what it's worth.
✔️ Same for gear a brand sends you for a video.
✔️ Keep a list before Dec 31: what you got, when, and its value.

Comment STREAM with your creator tax question.

Not affiliated with Rockstar Games. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: Got a Game Code for a Review? That Can Be Taxable Income
captions.youtube_description: Myth: a game code or gear a publisher sends you for a review is a gift. Fact: income paid in property or goods for your work must be reported, even with no 1099-K, 1099-MISC or W-2. Count it at its value and keep a list. Source: IRS 'All income is taxable, including gig economy and tip income'. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games. General information, not advice for your situation.
